title.en: How Vaccines Protect You and the People Around You

desc.zh: 疫苗里没有杀病毒的药，它凭什么让你少生病，又凭什么护住打不了针的婴儿？七个可以拖动的模型：和病毒赛跑、第二针为什么又快又多、防感染与防重症、“95% 有效”的算法、病例里为什么多数打过疫苗、需要多少人接种、保护消退。
desc.en: A vaccine contains no drug that kills the virus, so how does it keep you from getting ill, and how does it protect a baby too young for the jab? Seven models you can push: the race against the virus, why the second dose is faster and bigger, infection versus severe disease, what "95% effective" means, why most cases can be vaccinated people, the coverage needed, and waning.

title.zh: 初次免疫应答：和病毒赛跑
title.en: Primary immune response: the race against the virus

desc.zh: 病毒几个小时翻一倍，没见过它的 B 细胞从很低的起点扩增，一个多星期才追上；病已经生了。
desc.en: The virus doubles every few hours while naive B cells start from a tiny number and take over a week to catch up, by which time the illness has happened.

zh: 第一次感染为什么会病
en: why do you get sick the first time
how the immune system fights a virus

title.zh: 二次免疫应答与记忆细胞

desc.zh: 疫苗让免疫系统先打一场没有危险的仗，留下记忆细胞；第二次应答起点高，所以又快又多。抗体会消退，记忆细胞撑得久得多。
desc.en: A vaccine runs a safe first fight that leaves memory cells; the second response starts higher, so it is faster and larger. Antibodies fade; memory lasts much longer.

zh: 抗体测不到了还有免疫吗

title.en: Protection against infection vs severe disease

desc.zh: 抗体在门口拦，几个月就变薄；记忆细胞在里面追。所以打过疫苗的人仍可能被感染，但病毒涨得低、病得轻得多。
desc.en: Antibodies block at the door and thin out within months; memory cells chase from inside. So vaccinated people can still be infected, but the virus peaks lower and the illness is much milder.

zh: 打了疫苗为什么还生病
en: why do vaccinated people get sick
how long does vaccine protection last

title.zh: 疫苗效力：相对风险降低
title.en: Vaccine efficacy as relative risk reduction

desc.zh: 效力 = 1 − 两组发病风险之比，用随机对照试验的病例数算出；它不是“打了的人里有多少会生病”，也不告诉你绝对风险和不确定性。
desc.en: Efficacy = 1 − the ratio of the two arms' risks in a randomized trial. It is not the share of vaccinated people who fall ill, and it says nothing by itself about absolute risk or uncertainty.

title.zh: 病例里打过疫苗的比例

desc.zh: 接种率越高，病例里打过疫苗的人越多，哪怕疫苗很有效；接种率超过 1 ÷ (2 − 效力) 时，病例里就以打过疫苗的人居多。
desc.en: The higher the coverage, the more cases are vaccinated people, even with an effective vaccine; past coverage 1 ÷ (2 − efficacy) they are the majority.

en: does this mean the vaccine doesn't work

title.zh: 需要的接种率：阈值 ÷ 效力

desc.zh: 疫苗不完美时，挡住流行需要的接种率是 (1 − 1/R₀) ÷ 效力；超过 100% 时光靠这种疫苗挡不住。接种率越接近这个线，打不了针的婴儿越安全。
desc.en: With an imperfect vaccine the coverage needed to stop spread is (1 − 1/R₀) ÷ efficacy; above 100% this vaccine alone cannot do it. The closer coverage gets to the line, the safer the baby who cannot be vaccinated.

en: how many people need to be vaccinated to stop spread

desc.zh: 保护按半衰期消退，每个病例能传给的人数慢慢爬回 1 以上；回到 1 要多久按对数取决于余量，加强间隔要赶在它前面。
desc.en: As protection wanes, the number each case infects creeps back above 1; how long that takes depends logarithmically on the margin, and boosters must come before it.

en: how often do you need a booster

title.zh: 读懂疫苗数字的三个问题
title.en: Three questions for any vaccine number

desc.zh: 防的是什么、什么时候测的？跟谁比、分母是多少？够不够挡住传播？
desc.en: Protection against what, measured when? Compared with whom, out of how many? Enough to stop spread?
